schema_and_taxonomy.summary: Schema v2 source_locale en, revision 1, political-economy-markets with Brazil country geography and controlled topics/phenomena; new descriptive kind structural-economic-outlook registered as editorial line within existing programme, without taxonomy change.

source_vintage_and_cutoff.summary: As-of 3 November 2026 information cutoff. 2027 GDP, fiscal, inflation, currency and interest estimates explicitly labeled forecasts from institution-specific vintages. 2026 Jan-Sep trade and quarterly macro observations have dated source and do not masquerade as realised 2027 data.

factual_methodology.summary: Key institutional claims cross-checked: 2027 PLOA R$18.6bn full vs R$83.4bn adjusted primary estimates, target R$73.2bn and R$2.576tn primary ceiling (Planning Ministry); Selic Jan-Sep path 15,14.75,14.5,14.25,14,13.75 and BCB Sep GDP2027 1.4; Sept SPE GDP2027 2.3; Jul IMF 2.2 GDP2027 and 3.1 CPI; World Bank 1.7 GDP2027; Oct Prisma Fiscal R$44bn primary deficit and 87% DBGG; MDIC Jan–Sep export partners [84.68,44.15,27.46,11.58] USD bn; EU-Mercosur provisional May1 2026. Observed, forecast, budget appropriations, fiscal balance definitions and actual trade differentiated.

evidence_traceability.summary: Thirty matching primary and institutional original URLs in each locale across 17 distinct hosts, with source inventory at end and inline numbered citations. Verified central macro, fiscal, trade and treaty mechanisms from BCB, MPO, SPE, IMF, World Bank, MDIC, Council EU and government Prisma. Exhaustive line-by-line verification of each international source and every individual sector example is not possible in this review, so approval retains explicit sampling caveat.

research_depth.summary: EN approximately 9746 substantive words and PT-BR 11223, with 35 ordered analytical chapters plus bibliography, full national macro, banks/credit, regional trade blocs, sectors, infrastructure, institutions, AI, climate, and three conditional 2027 outlooks. Not a brief topical outline.

visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Three numeric charts in both languages: dated GDP forecast [1.2,1.4,1.7,2.2,2.3], observed Selic target series [15,14.75,14.5,14.25,14,13.75], and Jan–Sep 2026 country/region exports [84.68,44.15,27.46,11.58]; all paired exactly. Also table evidence >=31 Markdown rows, 1 causal flow and 1 geographic exposure map per language; labels distinguish units/vintages and selected destinations.

bilingual_equivalence.summary: Exact 35-section analytical structure, 30 identical bibliography URLs, equal chart values and source periods, equivalent scenario, balance sheet and fiscal caveats with fluent idiomatic Portuguese and English.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: Long-form institutional prose free from conversational instructions, duplicated meta descriptions, fabricated illustrative media, or electoral endorsement. Figures are source-backed and qualified; dates and causal links explicit.

contrary_evidence.summary: Forecast range not uncertainty band; adjusted PLOA surplus not full balance; China trade surplus not competitiveness guarantee; EU treaty provisional application not observed benefits; BRICS settlement systems not common currency.

counterfactual_review.summary: Three conditional paths and next-year monitoring signals explicitly identify criteria that would weaken investment recovery, fiscal credibility, disinflation and external-trade theses; no own probabilities assigned.

pipeline_validation.summary: Source-level validation reproduced structural thresholds and exact chart values, 30 link parity and registry kind registration. Full npm run build/validate-pipeline and downstream deployment must be established by GitHub CI; not attested here.

contrary_evidence: Forecasts range from 1.2% to 2.3% real GDP growth using different institutions, dates and model assumptions; none is a realised 2027 figure.
The 2027 draft budget's R$83.4 billion adjusted primary surplus differs from its R$18.6 billion full primary balance and should not be treated as the same fiscal outcome.
The EU–Mercosur interim trade agreement has been provisionally applied to Brazil since 1 May 2026, but measured investment and export effects require subsequent evidence.
China's large bilateral trade surplus does not identify Brazilian industrial competitiveness or future commodity prices.
BRICS payment interoperability and local-currency settlement are not a common currency or a unified capital market.
limitations: The 2027 budget remains a proposal as of the information cutoff; neither appropriation nor project pipeline constitutes executed spending.
2026 data from GDP, credit, fiscal and trade statistics have different observation dates and should not be presented as one synchronized monthly release.
GDP forecast vintages are shown for comparison, not as a statistical confidence interval or political performance ranking.
Underlying financial and market figures are from public institutional reporting and do not include firm-by-firm audited financial statements.
Conditional scenarios are not assigned subjective probabilities or invented GDP levels.
Fact checking concentrated on primary sources for headline quantitative claims and institutional claims; 30 source URLs catalogued but not all original sector studies read in full.
Comparison of institutional 2027 growth forecasts is illustrative and cannot be used as a statistically pooled forecast or confidence interval.
Complete npm build and static public output were not executed by the source connector; GitHub Actions must validate before treating the site as live.
notes: Editorial programme mapping fixed by adding a registered editorial-line kind, with no new taxonomy programme. Published report must preserve this precise schema-v2 snapshot and SHA-bound staging content.
